title: Iran ‘DIRTY BOMB’ Claims; Will Iran Change its Nuclear Posture? | Sina Azodi
author: Murtaza Hussain
content:
In this episode of the Drop Site News' The War Brief, Murtaza Hussain and
Sarmad Jawad examine reports alleging Iran could target Washington, D.C., and
claims that Iranian dams support underground missile cities.

They discuss the evidence cited in the reporting, the role of anonymous
intelligence leaks, and how claims about civilian infrastructure could shape
the case for escalating the conflict.

Later Sina Azodi, author of "Iran and the Bomb" and a historian of Iran's
nuclear program, joins The War Brief to discuss Iran's options after strikes
on its nuclear facilities.

Azodi outlines three possible paths: dismantling the program, secretly
crossing the threshold to build a nuclear weapon, or rebuilding nuclear
capacity while remaining a threshold state. He explains why he sees the third
path as most likely, why withdrawing from the Non-Proliferation Treaty would
not automatically mean Iran would build a bomb, and why a single nuclear
device may not provide a credible deterrent. The conversation also examines
Iran's nuclear program as a negotiating tool and the limits of its previous
deterrence strategy.
